Toyota Next Move
HackTX 2026 · Developer post
Toyota Financial Services · HackTX 2026

Turning a vehicle walkaround into a clear next step.

A guided iPhone inspection that makes evidence and uncertainty visible, then connects what the camera saw to one useful action.

Read time · 8 min   Status · Working MVP   Theme · Responsible AI

When a customer asks, “What is the smartest next move for me and my Toyota?”, the hard part is gathering the right evidence, understanding its limits, and acting with confidence.

Toyota Next Move is our prototype for that experience. It guides a non-expert through an exterior and interior vehicle inspection, turns captured evidence into an uncertainty-aware vehicle view, and is designed to combine visible findings with synthetic customer, vehicle, loan, and lease data to produce one plain-language recommendation.

The goal is a premium inspection tool that feels at home on an iPhone: open the camera, walk around the vehicle, see the scan build, review what was found, and leave with a useful next action.

The experience

The journey is deliberately short:

01Start Scan
02Guided coverage
03Evidence-backed map
04Findings
05Next Move
  1. Start Scan. The user taps once and moves around the vehicle.
  2. Guided coverage. The app evaluates camera frames and updates the next-area prompt as coverage is accepted.
  3. Evidence-backed map. Covered, partial, blocked, and unseen regions remain visible.
  4. Findings. Visible observations are designed to attach to surfaces with evidence, confidence, and uncertainty; a real surface anchor is a next integration step.
  5. Next Move. The intended product path combines findings with a synthetic customer and agreement profile and returns one clear action.

Unseen areas stay visibly unknown. A normal material state means no visible issue was found in captured evidence; it never means the vehicle is mechanically healthy.

Why coverage matters

A camera can only tell us about what it sees. Next Move models coverage across 12 regions: covered, partial, blocked, or unseen. Low-quality frames do not advance coverage, and absence of evidence cannot create a clean finding. Ambiguous views ask for more evidence or human review.

That uncertainty is part of the product. A partial scan is a result with a next action, not a failure to hide.

A local-first technical foundation

The prototype is a SwiftUI iOS vertical slice. AVFoundation supplies camera frames, while ARKit may provide tracking and pose signals. The capture layer emits scan-session and coverage records; the perception boundary consumes evidence references and emits findings; product logic produces a recommendation.

Live capture and deterministic replay are interchangeable inputs. The replay uses decoded Toyota video frames and fixed JSON fixtures, so development, judging, and QA can inspect the same scan repeatedly without a physical vehicle. Shared JSON contracts keep capture, perception, product logic, and QA aligned.

Where model perception fits

The optional perception bridge samples a JPEG no more than once every two seconds and sends it to a private backend. The backend returns bounded observations: vehicle presence, view usability, recognizable canonical regions, and short guidance.

The app requires two distinct consecutive observations at confidence 0.7 or higher before recording a region. The requested region is never sent as a hint. Uncertain responses cannot manufacture coverage. The bridge does not diagnose mechanical or safety conditions, and no image produces a hidden-health conclusion.

The reveal is an evidence state

The vehicle begins as a neutral gray model. As evidence accumulates, observed surfaces reveal their normal vehicle material. Partial coverage produces a partial reveal; unseen areas remain neutral; blocked or uncertain regions stay muted. Findings sit above that material as restrained surface accents.

The material communicates where evidence exists, while a finding communicates what the evidence shows. A polished Toyota-like asset, named surface anchors, and a geometry-conforming reveal are the next visual step.

What we learned building the MVP

Making replay first-class gave the team a reliable end-to-end demo while live capture and a production-quality vehicle asset mature. Treating limitations as data made recommendations more trustworthy. Keeping the recommendation downstream of evidence makes customer context and agreement joins explicit and testable.

What comes next

  • Verify continuous live progression on the current iPhone build.
  • Replace temporary geometry with a cleaned, high-quality Toyota-like asset.
  • Attach an evidence-backed finding to a real surface anchor.
  • Connect scan findings to synthetic customer, vehicle, and loan/lease scenarios.
  • Rehearse Start Scan → guided coverage → vehicle reveal → finding → personalized next move.

Toyota Next Move is a prototype, not a remote diagnostic system. It shows how careful capture, explicit uncertainty, and responsible AI can turn a vehicle walkaround into a decision a customer can understand.

Build the demo around evidence you can repeat.

For a repeatable demo, use deterministic replay. It intentionally includes covered, partial, and unseen regions so the vehicle map and recommendation show the complete uncertainty model. Keep backend secrets server-side and never ship an OpenAI API key in the iOS app.
